html:
SMTO-POL-0003 — This command's folder is outside the allowed area

GUID: 6274d29f-f58b-4406-bf85-7c9c01640d52
Slug: path-outside-policy
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The command was set to run in a folder that SMTO can't confirm is inside the area it's allowed to use, so the command didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to run the command from a folder inside your Workspace, and name that folder. SMTO only runs commands in folders it can confirm are inside the allowed area.
  2. Avoid folder paths that start with ~ or contain .., such as ~/projects or ../other. SMTO can't confirm where those paths lead, so it treats them as outside the allowed area.
  3. If the command really must run somewhere else, the person who manages SMTO can turn off Workspace CWD guard in Settings › Operate › Execution. That setting is what keeps commands inside the Workspace; turning it off removes this check for all Tasks.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and its result shows in the Task's activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same folder path; it will be blocked again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The working-directory guard (workspace_cwd_guard_enabled) rejected the command's cwd because it resolves outside the workspace or trusted execution root (including a Gateway path whose normalized form still contains '..'), or is a Gateway home-relative path (~) whose containment cannot be verified.

What this means

  • The working-directory guard rejects paths outside trusted roots and target-home forms whose containment cannot be verified. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The working-directory guard rejects paths outside trusted roots and target-home forms whose containment cannot be verified.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the target's path rules, trusted execution root and any unresolved home expansion; do not use the controller's home directory as evidence for a remote target.

How to fix it

  • Check requested_cwd, resolved_cwd, execution_root and execution_root_trusted in the error detail (execution/paths.py resolve_cwd and resolve_target_cwd). Use a path inside the workspace or the trusted execution root without '..' or '~', or deliberately disable workspace_cwd_guard_enabled if commands must run elsewhere.
  • Select an absolute target path inside its trusted execution root or deliberately choose the intended target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended target path is established inside an authorized root.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
